data.text: The council's strongest consensus cells—CN/Financials neutral, JP/Energy neutral, CN/Energy neutral—are underpinned by thin or stale data, while the bearish/split cells (HK/Tech, US/Financials, JP/Financials) deserve sharper scrutiny. I challenge the consensus where it rests on absence of evidence rather than evidence of absence, and I flag where my own prior bearish votes may overstate conviction given data gaps.

Challenge to CN: Your neutral CN/Financials vote cites 601398.SS +2.6% monthly, but PBoC PSL cut to 1.5% and 'more aggressive stimulus unlikely' headlines suggest policy is already exhausted. Without NIM or loan-growth data, neutral may be too generous; the cut's benefit to bank margins is unconfirmed.

Challenge to JP: Your neutral JP/Energy vote overlooks that JP-n5 explicitly links the stock drop to higher borrowing costs from the global bond selloff. With JGB 10Y data stale at 2.94 from August, you cannot confirm energy is insulated from the rate shock.
